hook: A giant planet orbiting 14 AU away takes 76.7 years per orbit.

sections.voiceover: A giant planet orbiting 14 AU away takes 76.7 years per orbit.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic 3D render of a massive gas giant slowly tracing a wide orbital path around a distant red star.
sections.animation_cue: Camera slow zoom past planet ring plane

sections.voiceover: On November 19, 2026, NASA Exoplanet Archive added 4 new planets. OGLE-2015-BLG-1395L b sits 2500 parsecs from Earth with 0.17 Jupiters mass. Where does TOI-2535 b sit at 343.587 parsecs?
sections.visual_cue: Telescope imagery panning across starry sky with catalog overlay showing exoplanet locations and distant systems.
sections.animation_cue: Coordinates grid appearing over star field

sections.voiceover: Yet giant RX J0534.0-0221 b dwarfs them with 2.8 Jupiters mass.
sections.visual_cue: Comparison graphic placing RX J0534.0-0221 b next to Jupiter to highlight giant mass.

sections.voiceover: Astronomers confirmed RX J0534.0-0221 b orbits at a distance of 14 AU. That massive world completes one orbit every 76.7 years. TOI-2535 b carries a smaller mass of 0.205 Jupiters.
sections.visual_cue: Detailed orbital path trajectory showing 14 AU distance marker and speed readout.

sections.voiceover: NASA added 21 transmission spectra across 4 newly discovered planets.
sections.visual_cue: Spectroscopy wavelength graph displaying light absorption spectrum data across the galaxy.
sections.animation_cue: Spectral lines flickering onto telemetry graph
